title: The Iron Uniform
premise: In 1905, in the garrison town of Velsk, Ulyana Zhou helps her father cut type in a print shop that has survived every regime by printing exactly what it is told. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the civil ledger containing every resident's name, Ulyana discovers the ledger is being rewritten to erase the dead, the disappeared, and anyone the new commandant finds inconvenient. With a disgraced army clerk, a widowed baker, and her father's failing eyesight, she secretly reprints the true ledger on stolen type, racing to distribute copies before the victors' historians seal the official record. The book ends with the shop burned and her father dead, but the true ledger already circulating in three cities—Ulyana, arrested and unbroken, knowing that ink outlives the men who burn it.
about_author: Z. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archival researcher who spent a decade cataloguing seized records from collapsed regimes across Eastern Europe. They write historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of official memory.

chapters.title: Lead and Ash
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A day in the print shop: setting type for the town's announcements, bantering with her father Anton, dodging the baker's son Kolya. She believes history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: warm, ironic contentment that the reader knows cannot last.

chapters.title: The Sound of Many Boots
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The army arrives at dawn; requisition notices are nailed to doors, and officers demand the shop print proclamations by nightfall. Anton complies without question—the family creed of invisibility. Emotional beat: dread masked as routine.

chapters.title: Commandant Reznik
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The commandant inspects the shop, charming and precise, and orders a special printing: a new town census ledger 'correcting' the old one. Ulyana notices names missing from his draft—including the miller's family, vanished last week. Emotional beat: first cold suspicion.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Wept
chapters.summary: Sasha's POV (introduced). Sasha, an army clerk ordered to transcribe the purge lists, drinks himself numb in the tavern and lets slip a fragment to Ulyana. He hates what he copies but fears desertion more. Emotional beat: complicity and shame.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Comparing the old civil ledger against Reznik's draft, she counts forty-one erased names—debtors, dissidents, the dead denied burial records. Her father urges silence; survival means invisibility. Emotional beat: the fracture between father and daughter begins.

chapters.title: Bread and Secrets
chapters.summary: Marina's POV (introduced). The widow Marina, whose brother is among the erased, feeds soldiers at her bakery and hears everything. She approaches Ulyana with a proposition: if the girl can print, the baker can hide and carry. Emotional beat: cautious alliance, grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Type Stolen in the Night
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She and Kolya smuggle lead type and a spare press stone into Marina's cellar. First test pages of the true ledger come out crooked but legible. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration—the first act of resistance.

chapters.title: The Commandant's Kindness
chapters.summary: Reznik's POV. The commandant dines with Anton, praising the shop's loyalty, revealing he knows Ulyana asks questions. He offers protection in exchange for the old ledger's plates. Emotional beat: menace wrapped in courtesy; power as seduction.

chapters.title: Anton's Choice
chapters.summary: Anton's POV. Torn between protecting his daughter and forty years of learned caution, he burns a page of the draft ledger rather than hand over plates—a small treason. Emotional beat: a father's love expressed through compromise.

chapters.title: Forty-One Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The cellar press produces its first full sheet of the true ledger. Sasha, now half-drunk half-desperate, brings them the remaining purge entries, crossing the line irrevocably. Emotional beat: the found family coheres around the table in candlelight.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Kolya's POV. A neighbor's boy sees the cellar light; Kolya confronts him and buys silence with bread and threats he doesn't feel. Paranoia spreads through the group; Marina wants to stop printing. Emotional beat: trust under strain.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Soldiers occupy the shop itself; Anton must print execution notices for three of the erased names. Ulyana sets the type with shaking hands, forced to cast the words of the men destroying her town. Emotional beat: humiliation, rage, the price of staying alive.

chapters.title: Sasha's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sasha's POV. Ordered to seal the official archive for transport to the capital, Sasha swaps one folder for a dummy and delivers the genuine purge correspondence to the cellar. Emotional beat: no way back; relief and self-loathing in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Distribution
chapters.summary: Marina's POV. Bread loaves hollowed with folded ledger sheets go out on the supply carts to three towns. Marina walks the route herself, passing checkpoints on nerve alone. Emotional beat: quiet heroism, the terror of ordinary errands turned subversive.

chapters.title: Reznik Closes In
chapters.summary: Reznik's POV. A copy of the true ledger reaches the commandant's desk. He understands instantly it was set on his own requisitioned type—and narrows the suspects to four. He chooses patience over arrests, laying a trap. Emotional beat: the hunter's calm.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Mill
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A supposed ally offers to take copies to the railway workers; it is Reznik's bait. Kolya insists on going instead of Ulyana and is taken. Emotional beat: guilt, helplessness, the cost of trusting too late.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Kolya's POV. Held in the guardhouse, Kolya gives them nothing—not because he is brave, but because he genuinely knows only fragments. Reznik realizes the boy is a dead end but keeps him as leverage. Emotional beat: endurance without glory.

chapters.title: Fire
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Soldiers torch the print shop with Anton inside—he refused to open the strongbox of type. Ulyana watches her childhood burn, clutching the last printed sheets. Emotional beat: devastation; the creed of invisibility dies with him.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Marina and Sasha's alternating POV. In the cellar they print the final run—five hundred copies of the complete true ledger—while patrols search house to house. Sasha volunteers to carry the master copy to the capital's newspaper men. Emotional beat: grim resolve; grief converted to deadline.

chapters.title: What Ink Outlives
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cornered at the bakery, Ulyana surrenders so Marina can escape with the distribution list. Before the arrest she hides the original plates in the flour store, trusting strangers she will never meet. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship—she becomes part of the record.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historians
chapters.summary: Reznik's POV. Interrogating Ulyana, the commandant finds no ledger, no plates, no accomplices he can prove. Reports arrive that copies have surfaced in three cities; the official record is already contested. He wins the town and loses the story. Emotional beat: pyrrhic victory, dawning futility.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, months later, in a prison work detail. A guard, bribed with nothing but curiosity, reads her a newspaper item: the true ledger entered evidence before a commission of inquiry, forty-one names restored to the record. She weeps once, then stands straighter. Emotional beat: hard-won hope—the truth got there first.
